title: Prism
description: Prism turns a Steam Deck into a living-room console: one home screen for Steam games, emulated games and, optionally, Plex movies and TV, with the habits of a real console.

modules.html:
A console, not a launcher

Prism boots straight into one home screen that holds your Steam games, your emulated games and, if you want, your Plex movies and TV. The design goal was to make a Steam Deck docked to a TV feel like a console: no desktop, no menus that assume a mouse, nothing to configure every time.

  • The Steam button opens a quick-menu card over any game: resume, save and load states, quit, sleep timer.
  • Controllers get player numbers in the order they're picked up, in every emulator, so local multiplayer just works.
  • Docking switches resolution and controls on its own, and the screen dims and sleeps without stopping downloads.
  • New games appear by themselves: install a Steam game or copy a ROM and it shows up within 15 minutes.
  • A rescue chord (hold L5 and R5) always gets you back home.

It's built on ES-DE with a small patch, its own theme and a set of background services that run in Steam's Game Mode.
